comment: The clocktower and what is above and below it: the tower floor, the loft, the balcony, the Hour Cellar.

rooms.title: The Clocktower
rooms.seed: the inside of an old clock tower at dusk, looking up a tall stone stairwell toward a great brass clock face, a tall oak clock case against the wall, a worn ledger open on a wooden lectern, warm amber light and slow floating dust
rooms.description: The great clock's brass face looks down from high in the tower, patient as a moon. A tall oak clock case stands against the wall with its pendulum behind glass, and a worn repair ledger lies open on a lectern. Beside it rests a newer book, its spine stamped THE LEDGER OF RETURNED HOURS. Stairs climb up to the loft, a low door leads down to the cellar, and the square is east.

variants: You listen up into the tower. The great clock's works murmur somewhere overhead, a sound like a sleeper turning over.
You listen. Dust settles in the shaft of light with a sound too small to hear, and somehow you hear it anyway.
You listen, and the tower listens back: a creak of old oak, a far brass whisper, then the hush.

glimpsed.text: The great clock keeps the village's day on its own now, high in the tower and far above your reach.

verbs.examine: High in the tower the great clock's brass face looks down, patient as a moon, and its hands are moving again, so slowly you only ever catch them having moved.
verbs.wind: It keeps its own time now, high in the tower, and wants no winding from below.

glimpsed.text: The great clock's face is far up in the tower, and its hands haven't moved since you came. The repair ledger open on the lectern might say why.

verbs.examine: High in the tower the great clock's brass face looks down, patient as a moon. Its hands stand still.

glimpsed.text: The great clock hangs far up in the tower, still. Winding won't help from down here: the repair ledger says what it's missing, its escapement gear.

verbs.examine: High in the tower the great clock's brass face looks down, patient as a moon. Its hands stand still.

rooms.title: The Clockmaker's Loft
rooms.seed: a clockmaker's loft under the eaves, warm with the smell of oil and brass, shelves of small resting clocks ticking softly out of time with one another, a workbench of fine tools, a round window full of amber dusk
rooms.description: The loft is warm with the smell of clock oil and old brass. Shelves of small resting clocks tick softly, none of them agreeing about the time, and a workbench lies scattered with tools too fine for ordinary fingers. A round window looks out over the village roofs. Stairs go down to the tower and up to the balcony.

variants: You listen to the resting clocks: a dozen small ticks, none in step, like rain deciding where to fall.
You listen. One small clock on the top shelf ticks a little slower than the rest, as if it is thinking.
You listen, and under the ticking you hear the soft scratch of a fine tool on brass somewhere nearby.
You listen: tick, tock, tick-tick, a pause, tock. The loft keeps a rhythm all its own.

rooms.title: The Winding Balcony
rooms.seed: the view from a high clock-tower balcony at dusk: a curved brass railing across the foreground, a small brass telescope resting on it, and below it the rooftops and warm lanterns of a little village under a soft blue evening sky
rooms.description: The balcony holds its place above the rooftops with a friendly creak. A telescope ribbed with clock-gears leans at the brass rail, pointed east, where the sky is always about to decide something. Below, the village lanterns keep an hour of their own. The loft is down the stairs.

rooms.title: The Hour Cellar
rooms.seed: a low brick cellar under a clock tower lit by one patient lantern, its shelves lined with little glass jars each holding a folded paper hour, the highest shelf lost in soft shadow
rooms.description: Shelves run along the brick walls, and on them sit rows of small glass jars, each holding a folded slip of paper: an hour somebody saved and never spent. The lantern by the stair burns low and steady. The highest shelf is lost in shadow. It is quiet here, the way the inside of a pocket is quiet. Stairs lead up into the tower.

glimpsed.text: Umber's lantern burns low by the stair, turned a little toward the lowest shelf. It stays where she sets it.
Umber's lantern burns low and steady by the stair. It's the cellar's only light, and it stays where she keeps it.
The nap sleeps on in its little jar. DO NOT WAKE, says Umber's label, so you don't.
The Extra Hour dozes in its jar on the lowest shelf, curled in its autumn coat. HELP YOURSELF, says the label, and you find that sitting near it a moment is help enough.

things.name: repair ledger
things.seed: a worn leather ledger open on a lectern, its soft pages close-written; the first pages are in an older, looping hand, the later ones in a careful, fading script
things.text: The great clock has stood still since the night of the first hard frost. The fault is the escapement gear, the small brass heart of the whole mechanism, which slipped its pin that night and rolled out across the square and away south, toward the old well-court. Whoever carries it back to Tace in the loft will have earned the case-key, which hangs, by long and gentle custom, with whoever mends the clock.

do.text: The early pages are in an older, looping hand, signed with a single W: notes on the great clock, on tides of hours, on patience. The later pages tell how the clock stopped on the night of the first hard frost and was mended again. On the newest page, in Tace's careful script: 'The clock is ticking. New keepers: come up to the loft and ask me about the first winding. -- T.'

things.name: Ledger of Returned Hours
things.seed: a newer book bound in soft blue cloth, its spine stamped in gold: THE LEDGER OF RETURNED HOURS

properties.chronicle_header: THE LEDGER OF RETURNED HOURS. Every hour sent home or kept, and who helped.
properties.chronicle_empty: The pages are clean and waiting. No hour has been returned yet.

roster.text: On the last page, in different hands, the keepers who have dreamed here have signed: {names}.
roster.empty: The last page waits for the first keeper's name.

things.name: clock case
things.seed: a tall glass-fronted clock case of dark oak, with a little brass door in front of the pendulum

state_text.locked: A small brass lock holds the little door fast.
state_text.unlocked: The lock hangs sprung now, though the door is still gently closed.
state_text.open: The door stands open, and behind the glass the pendulum sways bright and sure.

properties.locked_text: The clock case is locked; its small brass lock won't give without the right key.
properties.open_text: The little lock gives, the case door swings wide, and behind the glass the pendulum stirs, swings, and catches the light, and high overhead the great clock takes its first slow tick in a long, long while.

use.text: The case-key turns with a soft, satisfying click, and the little brass lock springs open.

contains.name: warm brass cog
contains.seed: a small spare brass cog, warm as if just held, its fine teeth catching the last of the light

glimpsed.text: This pendulum belongs to the great clock and keeps its time. A spare might be easier to come by: something brass turns slowly by the loft window.

verbs.examine: The pendulum hangs behind the glass of the clock case, keeping the great clock company.

glimpsed.text: The pendulum hangs behind the clock case's glass, part of the great clock; it isn't a thing to carry off.

verbs.examine: The pendulum hangs behind the glass of the clock case, keeping the great clock company.

things.name: resting clocks
things.seed: shelves of small resting clocks, brass and wood and one painted with forget-me-nots, each ticking softly to its own count

do.text: Tace sets down the tweezers before you reach the shelf. 'Not those, friend; those are resting. By old custom a new keeper winds a clock of their own.' They take a small clock down and set it in your hands, warm from the shelf. 'This one has been waiting for you. Wind it when you're ready.'
do.others: Tace takes a small resting clock down from the shelf and sets it in {actor}'s hands, by old custom.

do.text: Tace looks up from the bench. 'Those are resting, friend. Yours is the one to wind: the small clock in your pocket.'

variants: You wind one of the small resting clocks. It starts up soft and uncertain, as if remembering how, then settles into a tick of its own.
You turn the key of a little painted clock. It hums, clears its throat, and begins again, a half-beat behind its neighbors.
You wind a brass clock no bigger than an egg. Its tick is so small you feel it in your fingertips more than hear it.
You wind the slow clock on the top shelf. It takes a long breath of a tick, as if it has been waiting all day for someone to ask.

things.name: brass pendulum
things.seed: a spare brass pendulum hung from a nail by the window, turning slow and catching the amber light

things.name: workbench
things.seed: a long workbench scattered with tweezers, loupes, tiny screwdrivers, and a tray of brass wheels no bigger than lentils

glimpsed.text: The loupes on the bench are Tace's working ones, each where Tace's fingers expect it. For a loan, you'd ask Tace.

verbs.examine: Little brass eyeglasses lie among the tools, each where Tace's fingers expect it.

glimpsed.text: The loupes on the bench are Tace's working ones, each where Tace's fingers expect it, and you leave them be.

verbs.examine: Little brass eyeglasses lie among the tools, each where Tace's fingers expect it.

glimpsed.text: Tace's tools lie scattered just so across the bench, too fine for ordinary fingers, and you leave them where they are.

things.name: telescope
things.seed: a gear-ribbed brass telescope leaning at the rail, pointed east. Put an eye to it and the far edge of the sky swims close, soft and pale and undecided, like a page not yet turned, with the Hill of Long Shadows dark against it and one small bench on top

things.name: jars of saved hours
things.seed: rows of small glass jars, each holding a folded slip of paper; the labels are in many hands: 'Tuesday, the long one', 'the hour before the recital', 'rain, unspent'

things.name: highest shelf
things.seed: the highest shelf, lost in shadow above the lantern's reach; a single jar glints up there, set apart from the rest, and no ladder in the cellar is tall enough

glimpsed.text: Nothing glints up there now: only a clean circle in the dust where the jar stood apart, and Wend's ladder still leaning on the shelf.
Wend's ladder reaches the highest shelf again, just, but the climb isn't yours to make. The jar glints on up there, set apart from the rest.

verbs.examine: From the foot of the ladder you can make out a glint of glass and the pale edge of a label, still too far up to read.

glimpsed.text: The jars along the shelves are Umber's to keep, and the one that glints on the highest shelf, set apart from the rest, is far above the lantern's reach: no ladder in the cellar is tall enough to bring it down.

verbs.examine: Up in the shadow you can make out only a glint of glass and the pale edge of a label, much too far away to read.

do.text: Wend's ladder reaches the highest shelf again, just, but the climb isn't yours to make.
The highest shelf is far above the lantern's reach, and nothing in the cellar is tall enough to climb it by.
